method: Visual cross-check of printed grammar pp. 18–21 against vocabulary annotations; retain unresolved scope without generating unattested full forms.

decisions.evidence: Printed p. 18 §13(ii) gives tam-aya ‘their mother’ : tam-aya-v. This supports short aya in a possessed expression, but does not explicitly supply the independent plural or establish the scope of p. 49 -v across āya and aya.
decisions.decision: Retain both printed headword forms and the plural suffix annotation. Do not emit āyav or ayav from this ambiguous annotation. The compound grammar example remains supporting evidence, not a new vocabulary entry.

decisions.evidence: Printed p. 18 §13(vi) illustrates -kil after consonants, without choosing mar or marin. Printed p. 20 §15 says the nominative usually supplies the plural base; p. 21 §17(b) concerns case suffixes. These general rules do not resolve the vocabulary's alternative stems.
decisions.decision: Retain mar and marin and the printed -kil annotation. Do not select a base or generate both markil and marinkil without specific evidence.
